subject: SLO coverage mapping and fallback playbook for GreenBank (p50/p95)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@greenbank.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@greenbank.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO coverage and short-term carveouts for peak payment windows

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re working through procurement and need a concise mapping of how Redwood’s hosted API SLOs (p50 / p95) will apply to our account, plus a recommended fallback plan for predictable peak-days (e.g., month-end settlement and holiday spikes). Specifically: 

- Can Redwood provide the measured p50/p95 numbers you’ll commit to for our tenant in us-west-2, and how those are computed (measurement window, sampling, aggregation)?
- We expect 3–5 day seasonal bursts; can we request a temporary carveout to the p95 for up to 4 hours during a spike window without penalty? If so, what are the guardrails?
- If Redwood elects to route to a lower-cost model variant under load, what is the customer notification and fallback behavior?

Procurement needs a short playbook we can include with the contract: measurement definition, exception process, example emergency rollback steps. Can you send that over by COB Thursday? We’ll share it with security and legal.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Ops | GreenBank Payments
Attachments: none

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@greenbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO coverage and short-term carveouts for peak payment windows

Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks. I’ve pulled together a draft playbook and a proposed coverage matrix (attached) for GreenBank. Quick summary up front:

- Default hosted commitments (us-west-2): p50 = 15ms, p95 = 120ms for single-request text generation with typical token length <= 256. Measurement: rolling 1h buckets aggregated to daily percentile reporting (explainer in the matrix).
- Temporary carveouts: we can approve a temporary p95 relaxation for up to 4 hours per approved event, capped at 12 hours per calendar month across events. Carveouts are requestable via the SLA exceptions workflow (see playbook).
- Fallback behavior: automatic routing to a compatible, lower-capacity model variant (same family, quantized) with a grace notification to the customer. If the routed variant changes output shape or latency materially, we will auto-fallback to the last-working model for VIP endpoints.

I’ve attached: 
- slo-coverage-matrix.xlsx — ties our p50/p95 commitments to measurement windows and example burst carveouts.
- greenbank-slo-redlines-v1.pdf — wording we propose to include in the contract for exceptions and notification timelines.

Internal: Ben — can you confirm the p50/p95 numbers above are realistic for the committed dedicated pool we discussed? Marissa — I included the procurement-friendly language; any legal redlines you foresee?

I’ll be out of pocket Wed morning but can iterate post-lunch.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: slo-coverage-matrix.xlsx, greenbank-slo-redlines-v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO coverage and short-term carveouts for peak payment windows

Lauren / team —

Confirmed: the numbers in Lauren’s draft are achievable with the dedicated capacity config we discussed, with the following clarifications we should surface to GreenBank: 

- Measurement windows: we recommend rolling 1-hour buckets but exclude transient connection setup spikes (first-token latency) from p95 by using server-side warm-up windows for cold starts — this reduces false positives during rolling deploys.
- Carveout guardrails: carveouts will be approved only if Redwood is given a 48h notice for planned peaks. For emergency events (<48h notice) we can provide a one-time 4-hour operational carveout but it requires joint postmortem and a temporary credit if we miss the contracted p95 outside the carveout window.
- Routing behavior: automatic routing to a compatible quantized variant will preserve tokenization and primary output schema but may show <5% delta in model scoring metrics. For strict-regression-sensitive endpoints (payments risk analysis), we recommend enabling an explicit "no-variant-fallback" flag in the tenant config — this prevents automatic routing and triggers a routed-by-policy fallback to a different region instead.

I’ve added these notes to the spreadsheet (sheet: engineering-notes).

—Ben
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Sep 2025 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO coverage and short-term carveouts for peak payment windows

Team —

I reviewed the proposed commitments and the carveout gating. Approve moving forward with this language conditionally:

1) Add a telemetry clause that grants Redwood access to anonymized latency traces for any approved carveout event (for 30 days) to validate root cause.
2) Add a throughput cap for any approved carveout: we will cap sustained concurrency to the committed burst profile (we must avoid arbitrary unlimited bursts).
3) Include an emergency rollback play: if GreenBank flags >0.5% accuracy/regression deviation after a fallback routing, Redwood will immediately revert traffic and provide expedited remediation.

If Sales/legal want this reflected differently in the contract wording, tell me and I’ll provide a short tech annex. Otherwise, Lauren — feel free to share the attachments and the updated matrix with GreenBank; mark the carveout approvals as "subject to final telemetry/throughput annex."

-Markus
VP, Serving Runtime

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@greenbank.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@greenbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO coverage and short-term carveouts for peak payment windows

Elena —

Attached is the GreenBank SLO playbook and our proposed contract redlines (greenbank-slo-redlines-v1.pdf) plus the coverage matrix (slo-coverage-matrix.xlsx). Key points captured for procurement: 

- Committed targets (us-west-2): p50 15ms, p95 120ms (rolling 1h buckets, aggregated daily).
- Approved carveouts: up to 4 hours per approved event, 12 hours per month total; 48h notice requested for planned events; single emergency 4h allowance available under joint-ops agreement.
- Telemetry and throughput annex: carveouts are subject to a telemetry access clause (30 days of anonymized traces) and a capped sustained concurrency during the carveout window.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a compatible model variant, with a "no-variant-fallback" tenant flag option for risk-sensitive endpoints. If a fallback creates measurable regression (>0.5%), Redwood will roll back immediately and follow an expedited remediation plan.

Next steps: If this aligns, please confirm and we’ll include the two attachments as a contract annex and route the DocuSign link for the SLA addendum. We can also schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough for your ops team.

Thanks — Lauren
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
